notes: Contact page per docs/research/07-recommendations-and-brief.md section 5: a short form, a modest response-time promise, direct channels, an urgent route by phone and the legal entity block. The EnquiryForm component looks fields up by name (name, company, role, email, phone, engineFamily, need, message), so the field names below are fixed. The form takes no attachment; the attachment note is the message field's hint, which the component renders under the textarea. Values shown here come from the research dossier; the phone number is the one site.json carries. No map: 01 section 1 indicates a domicile address at Bahnhofplatz, and 07 section 5 says map only if there is an office.
clientToConfirm: WhatsApp: no WhatsApp channel is rendered on this page because site.json company.whatsapp is empty. The documented link (wa.me/41764186350) is on +41 76 418 63 50, not on the primary number +41 76 595 88 61 (01 section 8; 07 section 10 item 4). Confirm which number carries WhatsApp; it must equal company.phone, and then site.json company.whatsapp and a WhatsApp channel here are set together. 07 section 8 also recommends a WhatsApp Business profile.
Response-time promise: the page promises a reply within one working day, Monday to Friday, Swiss time. Confirm that the inbox and the phone are monitored to that standard and who replies.

Primary phone: +41 76 595 88 61 is used throughout (hero and contact page since April 2026; site.json). Two other numbers are in circulation: +41 76 418 63 50 (header button and WhatsApp link) and +41 76 358 84 90 (Swiss Aerospace Cluster directory). Confirm the one number.

Out-of-hours cover: the urgent route says call rather than write and makes no 24-hour promise. Confirm whether calls are answered outside Swiss working hours and whether a 24-hour AOG line should be promised (05 section 5 item 6 recommends one).

Attachments: the form has no upload; visitors are told to send files by email after the first reply. Confirm this is acceptable, or ask for a file-upload field (07 section 5 and section 8 recommend one) once a storage and virus-scanning route exists.
Calendar booking: 07 section 5 and section 8 recommend a booking link (Cal.com or Calendly) with a named consultant. None is documented, so none is shown. Supply a booking URL if wanted.

Privacy notice: the consent text points to the privacy notice for FADP and GDPR rights. The notice must name the actual processors (Cloudflare through the Higgsfield hosting platform and the email provider that delivers the form). Confirm the email provider used at launch.

title: Talk to us
intro: Tell us the engine, where it is, what is planned and by when. We reply within one working day.

form.title: Send us a workscope or a question
form.responsePromise: We reply within one working day, Monday to Friday, Swiss time. For anything urgent, call rather than write.

fields.name: message
fields.label: Message
fields.hint: Tell us the engine type or serial number, where it is, what is planned and the date. This form takes no attachments: after our first reply, send workscopes, borescope reports or records by email.

form.consentText: I agree that Flight Hour Solution GmbH may use these details to answer my enquiry and follow it up. The form reaches us as an email; nothing is stored on the website. I can withdraw consent at any time by writing to contact@flighthoursolution.com. My rights under the Swiss FADP and the GDPR are in the privacy notice.
form.successTitle: Thank you. We have your enquiry.
form.successText: We reply within one working day, Monday to Friday, Swiss time. If you have a workscope, a borescope report or a records pack to share, reply to our email with the files attached. If the matter is urgent, call +41 76 595 88 61.
form.source: Form contents per docs/research/07-recommendations-and-brief.md section 5 (name, company, role, engine type, need, message, attachment, response-time promise) and docs/research/05-competitor-benchmark.md section 6 (short form with a visible response-time promise). Processing facts in the consent and success texts: site/README.md, Switches and secrets (the form calls a server function that emails the enquiry to the company, or opens the visitor's email program; no personal data is stored on the server) and site/content-brief/VOICE-AND-FACTS.md, Legal (FADP and GDPR; the contact form sends an email; no analytics, no marketing cookies). Legal entity name in the consent text: docs/research/01-company-profile.md section 1.
form.notes: Required fields match what the component and the server function enforce (name, company, email, message and consent); role, phone, engine family and need are optional and the component labels them so. The one-working-day promise is a commitment the client must confirm, not a research fact; it is listed in clientToConfirm at the top of the file.
